units.function: Normalizes package paths by converting backslashes, stripping leading relative/absolute markers, removing dot segments and lexically popping parent segments.
units.dependencyDirection: A dependency-free utility imported broadly by company portability, company Skills, Skills catalog and teams catalog services; policy-sensitive callers all depend outward on the same permissive normalization semantics.
units.keyDataModels: Unbranded input and output path strings with no typed provenance, trust level, platform, validation result or rejected-reason model.
units.lifecycle: Transform separators; strip leading ./ and /; split; discard empty/dot segments; pop accumulated segments for ..; join remaining segments.
units.testAssessment: No direct focused test file was found by symbol search. Behavior is exercised indirectly by previously audited portability and Skills suites, but adversarial absolute, drive-letter, UNC, NUL, Unicode-normalization and collision cases are not owned by this unit.
units.designRationale: Produce stable slash-separated relative-looking paths across operating systems and tolerate imperfect package input.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs canonical package paths, but untrusted path validation must distinguish normalization from rejection and must make collisions explicit before any lookup, extraction or write.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT as a typed canonical-path parser that rejects absolute/UNC/drive paths, root escapes, control/NUL characters, invalid Unicode and ambiguous normalized collisions; return stable error codes and use separate APIs for trusted local relative paths versus untrusted package entries.
units.responsibilityConflict: Silent path reinterpretation can cause the reviewed package path set and the applied path set to differ, invalidating approval digests and evidence about exactly which content was imported.

symbol search found broad consumers but no direct focused test owner
securityFindings: Leading / and excess .. are silently clamped instead of rejected, so malicious and benign paths can canonicalize to the same output.
Windows drive and UNC semantics are not rejected; C: remains a segment after backslash conversion.
Control characters, NUL, Unicode normalization/case collisions and reserved platform names are not checked.
The function returns an ordinary string and cannot prove whether normalization was lossless or policy-safe.
